To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MSWI fly ash particles are mainly composed of calcium and silicon compounds.
the MSWI fly ash particles contain CuCl and CuO and that the particles containing Cu are formed in a condensation process.
the MSWI fly ash particle surface is covered by copper chloride, iron oxide, and zinc oxide.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the mechanisms that govern the formation of the MSWI fly ash particles.
the identification of the mechanisms that control the formation of submicron particles in the MSWI flue gases.
the identification of the chemical species of the most relevant elements in fly ash.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the metal distribution on the particles surface depends on the chemical speciation of the metal, the particle size and the chemical speciation.
the distribution of the metals in MSWI fly ash is mainly due to the condensation of the gaseous species.
the distribution of metals in the MSWI fly ash depends on the chemical form of the metal, the chemical form of chlorine, and the particle size.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chlorine is mainly concentrated on the particle surface, whereas iron, zinc, and copper are distributed throughout the particles.
the particle size distribution of MSWI fly ash is a good indicator of the metal speciation.

the metal accumulation on particles of MSWI fly ash is mainly due to heterogeneous condensation of volatile metals and that the presence of copper chloride on the surface of fly ash particles may be due to the formation of copper chloride particles during heterogeneous condensation processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of morphological, compositional, and leaching test results allows a better understanding of the metal behavior in MSWI fly ash.
the particle size distribution is a significant factor in determining metal distribution.
the particle size distribution and morphology of fly ash can be used to infer the mechanism of formation of the particles.
